fork.note: LOCAL-FIXTURE ONLY (scripts/official/empty_rpc.py, empty state) — NOT a mainnet-fork replay. block_number is a non-zero placeholder (approx. Ethereum height on 2021-08-10) required by the runner. The incident spanned Ethereum, BSC and Polygon; the fixture uses a representative source->dest pair.

contracts.note: Minimal reconstruction; no production addresses asserted. Funds were returned by the attacker.

root_cause_summary.vulnerable_pattern: EthCrossChainManager.verifyHeaderAndExecuteTx executed the contract/method named in a cross-chain message with no restriction, so a message could target the owner-only EthCrossChainData.putCurEpochConPubKeyBytes (ECCM owns ECCD) and replace the consensus keeper.
root_cause_summary.privilege_chain: ECCM is owner of ECCD; the owner-only keeper setter was reachable via a cross-chain message.
root_cause_summary.two_steps: 1) replace keeper via a relayed message targeting ECCD; 2) as the new keeper, submit a header directly and forge fromContract = the registered source proxy so LockProxy.unlock pays out.
root_cause_summary.selector_collision: The real attacker brute-forced a method string (f1121318093(bytes,bytes,uint64)) whose selector collides with putCurEpochConPubKeyBytes(bytes). This model keeps the function name, dispatches by bytes4(keccak256(method)), and represents the keeper by its authorised submitter address.
root_cause_summary.fix: Restrict which contracts/methods a cross-chain message may invoke (Poly added callable-contract/method whitelists); modelled as forbidding messages that target ECCD.

exploit_characteristics.style: arbitrary cross-chain call reaches privileged keeper setter; keeper replacement then forged unlock
exploit_characteristics.notes: ~$611M across Ethereum, BSC and Polygon; funds subsequently returned. No private key was leaked.
